tests.name: existence
tests.description: The Existence functions: empty(), exists([criteria]), all(criteria), allTrue(), anyTrue(), allFalse(), anyFalse(), subsetOf(other), supersetOf(other), count(), distinct(), isDistinct(); and what FHIR's FHIRPath page says about which FHIR elements exist. Leaves out what the text does not settle: non-Boolean items given to allTrue() and its kin, a criteria that yields a non-Boolean or several items in all(), equality between items of different types, equality of quantities that needs unit conversion (optional in both versions), the order distinct() returns, and which of two equal items it keeps.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-004
group.description: exists() without criteria is true if the input has any item, false if it is empty
group.source: Returns `true` if the collection has any elements, and `false` otherwise. This is the opposite of `empty()`, and as such is a shorthand for `empty().not()`. If the input collection is empty (`{ }`), the result is `false`.
Returns `true` if the input collection has any items (optionally filtered by the criteria), and `false` otherwise.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-005
group.description: exists(criteria) is where(criteria).exists(): true if the criteria is true for some item, false if it is false or empty for every item or the input is empty
group.source: The function can also take an optional criteria to be applied to the collection prior to the determination of the exists. In this case, the function is shorthand for `where(criteria).exists()`.

Returns a collection containing only those elements in the input collection for which the stated `criteria` expression evaluates to `true`. Elements for which the expression evaluates to `false` or empty (`{ }`) are not included in the result.
If the input collection is empty (`{ }`), the result is empty.
Using the optional criteria can be considered a shorthand for `where(criteria).exists()`.
If one or both of the arguments is an empty collection, a comparison operator will return an empty collection.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-006
group.description: exists(criteria) signals an error when the criteria evaluates to more than one item for an item, as where() does: 2.0.0 calls exists(criteria) a shorthand for where(criteria).exists(), 3.0.0 says it can be considered one, and both versions' where() signal the error
group.source: In this case, the function is shorthand for `where(criteria).exists()`.

If the result of evaluating the condition is other than a single boolean value, the evaluation will end and signal an error to the calling environment, consistent with singleton evaluation of collections behavior.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-007
group.description: The criteria of exists() and all() is evaluated for each input item with $this set to the item and $index to its 0-based position
group.source: If the function takes an `expression` as a parameter, the function will evaluate the expression passed for the parameter with respect to each of the items in the input collection. These expressions may refer to the special `$this` and `$index` elements, which represent the item from the input collection currently under evaluation, and its index in the collection, respectively.
Unless specified otherwise by the underlying Object Model, the first item in a collection has index 0.
The `criteria` argument is evaluated for each item (setting `$this` and `$index` before each iteration); if any return `true` then the function returns `true`, otherwise `false`.

The `criteria` argument is evaluated for each item (setting `$this` and `$index` before each iteration); if all return `true` then the function returns `true`, otherwise `false`. An empty input collection returns `true`.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-008
group.description: The 2.0.0 worked examples of exists() hold on the example Patient (three names, one identifier with use usual, a mobile phone telecom, no generalPractitioner)
group.source: Patient.name.exists() Patient.identifier.exists(use = 'official') Patient.telecom.exists(system = 'phone' and use = 'mobile') Patient.generalPractitioner.exists($this is Practitioner)
The first example returns `true` if the `Patient` has any `name` elements.
The second example returns `true` if the `Patient` has any `identifier` elements that have a `use` element equal to `'official'`.
The third example retruns `true` if the `Patient` has any `telecom` elements that have a `system` element equal to `'phone'` and a `use` element equal to `'mobile'`.
And finally, the fourth example returns `true` if the `Patient` has any `generalPractitioner` elements of type `Practitioner`.

source.section: Propagation of empty results in expressions

group.source: If any operand to a single-input operator or function is an empty collection, the result is an empty collection.

This means that if the evaluation for an element results in the empty collection (`{ }`), no element is added to the result, and that if the input collection is empty (`{ }`), the result is empty as well.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-019
group.description: subsetOf(other) is true when every input item is in other, true for an empty input whatever other is, and false for a non-empty input when other is empty
group.source: Returns `true` if all items in the input collection are members of the collection passed as the `other` argument.

Conceptually, this function is evaluated by testing each element in the input collection for membership in the `other` collection, with a default of `true`. This means that if the input collection is empty (`{ }`), the result is `true`, otherwise if the `other` collection is empty (`{ }`), the result is `false`.
Merge the input and other collections into a single collection without eliminating duplicate values.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-020
group.description: subsetOf() decides membership with the = operator: case-sensitive for strings, trailing decimal zeroes ignored, complex values compared child by child
group.source: Membership is determined using the <<equals>> (`=`) operation.
`String`: comparison is based on Unicode values
`Decimal`: values must be equal, trailing zeroes after the decimal are ignored
For complex types, equality requires all child properties to be equal, recursively.

group.name: REQ-EXISTENCE-035
group.description: When exists() or all() is nested inside the criteria of another, $this and $index refer to the outer item again once the nested call is complete (stated only in 3.0.0)
group.source: Variables introduced by scoped functions can only be accessed within the specified parameters of the scoped function. This behavior is preserved through nesting, meaning specifically that once a nested scope function evaluation is complete, the variables in the outer scoped function are again available.
